answer: Submissions that land within 121 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The quartz detector writes to horizon, and bridge exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, and thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 197 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 4 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
